quotes.DEC-8: DEC-8 (registers/DECISIONS.md:19, 2026-09-27, AUTHOR): "ETT, causal openness is two-sided: `def:causally_open_spacetime_open` is read with `J^±`. `CausallyOpen` is the definition, and `prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality` is closed as stated"; notes: "rules OQ-9; answer \"Both: J±\"; the paper's definition gains a `±` when it is next edited"
quotes.printed_definition: def:causally_open_spacetime_open (ETT.tex:694-697): "Let $M$ be a topological spacetime. The causality of $M$ is open, and $M$ is causally open, if for every open subset $\U$ of $M$ and every open subset $\V\subset \U$ the set $J^+_\U(\V)$ is open."
quotes.tarentin_ii_i_proof: ETT.tex:741-747: "Let $a,b\in \W$. Since the causality of $M$ is open, for every $i\in I$, J(a,b) = J^+(a)\cap J^-(b) \subset J^+(\ring J^+(a_i)) \cap J^-(\ring J^-(b_i)) = \ring J^+(a_i)\cap \ring J^-(b_i) = \ring J (a_i,b_i)" -- the step J^-(\ring J^-(b_i)) = \ring J^-(b_i) (l.745-746) needs J^-_M of an open set to be open.

labels.label: T-abs-gateline-local/3-causally-open-future
labels.notes: gateLine_causallyOpenFuture : gateLine.CausallyOpenFuture is the printed definition, for EVERY U and every open V ≤ U. gateLine_isOpen_Jplus has no hypothesis on U or V beyond V ≤ U. Through isOpen_sum_iff, the inr-preimage is open because Unit is discrete (isOpen_discrete). The inl-preimage is rewritten by gateLine_preimage_inl_Jplus, stated for every U and every SET A, so A may contain ⋆: ⋆ ≤_U inl b is False, so ⋆ contributes nothing to the line part. It becomes timelikeLine.Jplus (trace U) (trace V), open by timelikeLine_causallyOpen_of_chronalNeighbours.1 (Causal/LadderLocal.lean:476). The case 'V ∋ ⋆' and the case 'U without the gate inl 5' are therefore both covered.

labels.label: T-abs-gateline-local/4-not-causally-open
labels.notes: gateLine_Jminus_star : gateLine.Jminus ⊤ {inr ()} = inl '' Iic 10 ∪ {inr ()} (checked by #check). This is J⁻_M({⋆}) = (−∞,10] ∪ {⋆}: inl a ≤_⊤ ⋆ iff a ≤ 10. gateLine_not_isOpen_Jminus_star takes V = gateStar = {⋆}, open, and U = ⊤. An open J⁻ would make Iic 10 clopen in ℝ (isClopen_iff), which is refuted at 10 and at 11. gateLine_not_causallyOpen (¬ CausallyOpen, DEC-8) and gateLine_not_causallyOpenPast (¬ gateLine.dual.CausallyOpenFuture, the past half alone) both apply it at (⊤, gateStar, le_top).

labels.label: T-abs-gateline-local/5-locally-causally-open
labels.notes: gateLine_locallyCausallyOpen : gateLine.LocallyCausallyOpen, the two-sided node (LadderLocal.lean:152, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture ∧ dual.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture), through locallyCausallyOpen_iff with one neighbourhood for both sides. The future side holds on every open (gateLine_isOpen_Jplus). The past side holds on every U ≤ the line (missing ⋆) or U ≤ {⋆} (missing inl 5), by gateLine_isOpen_Jminus, whose preimage lemma is correct: inl a ≤_U ⋆ needs both ⋆ and inl 5 in U.

paper_findings_check: (1) Strict weakness: TRUE in the library's reading of defi:causalite. The gated line has CausallyOpenFuture and not CausallyOpen (Lean-checked). It is qualified under findings[0]. (2) The (ii)⇒(i) proof of prop:tarentin_topological_spacetime_causality uses J⁻: TRUE. ETT.tex:745-746 equates J^-(\ring J^-(b_i)) with \ring J^-(b_i), which needs J^-_M(open) open. This is the premise OQ-9 already recorded ('the proof ... uses J^-_U(V) open as well'), so it is not new. Wording is addressed under findings[1]. (3) Sharpness of prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal (DEC-8 reading: locally two-sided causally open without absolute minimality does not give causally open): TRUE and correctly worded as sharpness. It is not shown, and not claimed, for the printed J⁺ reading of that proposition, since the gated line is causally open in the future. Sibling T-abs-pushup-not-open's jumpLine gives the same sharpness in both readings, so the master should record two witnesses, not two discoveries. (4) Sharpness of lem:pushup_local (causal arc-connectedness cannot be dropped): TRUE, and the REPORT itself says 'a sharpness remark, not a defect'.

findings.what: The headline finding for the author ('DEC-8's ± is therefore a change of the notion, not a restatement') rests on the library's gluing-free reading of defi:causalite, the 'Equivalently' form, ETT.tex:245-251 (kb/0014). The finding does not say so. The gated line is NOT absolutely minimal (the REPORT discloses this, but only in findings[1] and the SCOPE, as a limitation on prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal). Whether the sheaf clause of defi:causalite means gluing, which is absolute minimality, is exactly OQ-18 (registers/DECISIONS.md:174), still OPEN. Under a gluing reading the gated line is not a causality of the paper, and the finding as evidenced would not apply. The Lean result is correct. Only its scope, as put to the author, is incomplete. The same omission was recorded as minor in T-ett-deux-pushup AUDIT-1.
findings.fix: In the finding and in SCOPE bullet 4, say 'in the library's (gluing-free, "Equivalently") reading of defi:causalite (kb/0014); under the gluing reading asked in OQ-18 (open) the gated line is not a causality'. Attach it to OQ-18 as one more consequence and open no new OQ. Optionally make the finding independent of the reading with an absolutely minimal witness. This is an auditor's sketch, not in Lean. On ℝ put x ≤_U y iff (x = y ∈ U) or (0 ≤ x ≤ y and [x,y] ⊆ U), and ≪_U = ∅. Absolute minimality follows by subdividing [x,y] for any cover. J⁺_U(V) is open for every open V ⊆ U: a witness x ∈ V with [x,y] ⊆ U gives (x, y+ε) ⊆ J⁺_U(V). But J⁻_ℝ((1,2)) = [0,2) is not open. That would show the printed form strictly weaker than DEC-8's among absolutely minimal causalities too. It is not locally causally open at 0, so it does not replace the gated line's other conjuncts.

findings.where: scaffold/CausalScaffold/GateLineLocal.lean:67-73 (SCOPE bullet 'Both non-implications need a non-local causality')
findings.what: The two non-implications are locally_causally_open ⇏ causally_open and locally_push_up ⇏ push_up. The bullet says both need a NON-LOCAL (not absolutely minimal) witness. The justification it cites does not give that for the second. lem:pushup_local only shows that a witness of the second must fail to be causally arc-connected, and causally_arc_connected ⇒ absolutely_minimal goes the wrong way. The claim appears to be TRUE by an argument the module does not give (auditor's sketch, not in Lean). On a T1 space, absolutely minimal ∧ locally_push_up ⇒ push_up. To see this, generate y ≤_U z by a chain y_i ≤_{U⊓O_i} y_{i+1} in push-up opens. Then regenerate each x ≪_U y_i with the cover {O_i, {y_i}ᶜ}. The last ≪-step into y_i must lie in O_i, and push-up in O_i moves it to y_{i+1}. This is the device of interpolatesOn_of_absolutelyMinimalOn and kb/0041. If it holds, it is a stronger ladder edge than lem:pushup_local's form, and the [[fails]] entry 3 note should cite it.
findings.fix: Either reword to 'the first needs a causality that is not absolutely minimal (AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpen_of_locallyCausallyOpen), the second one that is not causally arc-connected (lem:pushup_local)', or prove absolutely_minimal ∧ locally_push_up ⇒ push_up (T1) and cite it. The latter is a candidate [[implies]] for the keeper.
